transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I don’t enjoy my classes or my art anymore, and the things that used to excite me just feel flat and pointless. I just feel like I'm going through the motions and can't find any joy in them.
Have you had other times in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest like this for at least two weeks before this current period? If so, how many separate episodes have you had?
No, I've never experienced feelings like this before this current period. This is the very first time I've ever felt this way.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without a clear trigger? If there was a stressor, what was it?

Yes, they started about eight months ago when I was passed over for a tenure-track promotion that I had worked incredibly hard for. That disappointment, combined with a heavier teaching load and a lot of pressure at work, seemed to trigger everything. I've been feeling this way steadily ever since.
At your lowest points, have you had thoughts of ending your life, or have you ever heard or believed things that others said were not real? This helps me understand how severe the depression may be.

On my worst days, I do sometimes catch myself wishing I just wouldn't wake up or that I could quietly slip away, but I have absolutely no plans or intent to act on those thoughts. I've never heard or believed things that aren't real, though.

Even when work stress is lighter, do your low mood and loss of interest stay about the same, or do they clearly improve when the stress around the promotion and teaching load eases? Have these symptoms spread into most areas of your life, not just work?

Yes, they stay about the same; even when the stress is lighter or something good happens, this heavy, hollow sadness just doesn't lift. It has definitely spread beyond work into my personal life, as I've completely lost my passion for painting and my husband has had to take over most of the household chores because I just don't have the energy to keep up.

final_diagnosis.reason: This is a first depressive episode with persistent depressed mood/anhedonia for about 8 months, spreading across work and personal life, with functional impairment and passive death wishes but no psychotic symptoms. The syndrome is not limited to a stress reaction because symptoms persist even when stress lightens and involve multiple life domains. Based on the interview, the presentation is most consistent with a moderate depressive episode.
